newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: C&P aims to dominate middle-income housing.
newsitem.headline: C&P aims to dominate middle-income housing.

text.p: Low-cost residential builder C&P Homes Inc aims to become the leader in the middle-income housing sector in the coming years, C&P chairman Manuel Villar said on Wednesday.
"In the future, we hope to dominate the middle-income housing segment the way we dominated the low-cost housing segment," Villar said.
He said the rising per capita income of Filipino families would provide a good opportunity for the company to build higher-priced houses to meet growing demand.
Several middle-income residential villages would be launched in the coming months, particularly on the fringes of Manila.

C&P is the biggest socialised and low-cost housing developer, selling more than 23,000 units last year. Socialised houses are those which cost 180,000 pesos or less, while low-cost houses are those priced between 180,000 to 500,000 pesos.
Middle-income houses are those priced between one million and four million pesos per unit. The company started to venture into middle-income housing in 1993.
In the first quarter of the year, sales of middle-income housing units comprised only eight percent of the total unit sales, but contributed 34 percent of revenues.
The company reported a first quarter net income of 659 million pesos, up from 548 million in the same period last year.
Net real estate sales reached 2.04 billion pesos as against 1.70 billion pesos in the first quarter last year.
The company said it was expecting net income to rise to 3.1 to 3.2 billion pesos this year.
Villar, however, said the company's main thrust would still be on low-cost and socialised housing despite the new direction.
"We are going into the middle-income housing segment ... in addition to our socialised and low cost houses," he added.

Aside from houses, C&P is also building community shopping malls in residential villages as a value-added service. A new subsidiary would be created to handle the construction and operation of the commercial areas.
